title: Individual Unemployability under Disability Compensation
content:
Individual unemployability can be granted on a Disability Compensation award only when the award's tier is one at which the schedular thresholds can be met and the veteran has:

- one service-connected disability rated 60 percent or more, or
- two or more disabilities, with at least one rated 40 percent or more and a combined rating of 70 percent or more,

and is unable to secure substantially gainful employment. Employment with annual earned income at or below the marginal-income threshold is marginal and does not bar the grant.

When granted, the award is paid at the individual unemployability rate while the tier is unchanged. Individual unemployability is not available at the 100 percent tier.

**Schedular combinations (hypothetical disability pictures)**

| Disabilities | Meets the schedular thresholds |
|---|---|
| One disability at 60 percent | Yes |
| One disability at 50 percent, nothing else | No |
| Two disabilities, 50 percent and 40 percent, combined 70 percent | Yes |
| Two disabilities, 30 percent each, combined 50 percent | No — none at 40 percent and combined below 70 percent |
| Three disabilities, highest 30 percent, combined 70 percent | No — none rated 40 percent or more |

**Income illustration (hypothetical, with the 15650.00 threshold).** A veteran earning 12000.00 a year in part-time work is in marginal employment, which does not bar the grant; a veteran earning 30000.00 a year is not.

**Tier illustration.** An award at Disability Compensation (70% Combined Rating) granted individual unemployability is paid at the individual unemployability rate and still carries Disability Compensation (70% Combined Rating).
